top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on a specific conceptual step, the magic-wavelength lattice that removes the clock-transition light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated with suppressed Doppler and recoil shifts, plus its realisation at the 10^-18 level. It is reproduced with Sr, Yb and Hg in several laboratories, has a stable interpretation, and the two names map cleanly onto concept (Katori) and record realisation (Ye). The citation can be drawn narrowly enough to leave the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, ion clocks and other lattice groups outside it. The overlap with earlier metrology prizes and my distance from atomic physics remain real limits. P002 is a respectable second: a quantitative flat-band prediction followed by a reproduced experimental discovery, but the credit gap (Cao outside the three names) and the unsettled pairing mechanism eight years on make it less mature than P001. I prefer an award to no award, so P000 is last.
